package_info.package_name: MageCart JavaScript Skimmer (Euro Cup and Olympics Ticket Reseller)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (injected code, not a versioned package)
package_info.why_malicious: The injected JavaScript code is designed to steal payment card details from users of the ticket reseller website, exfiltrating sensitive financial information to attacker-controlled infrastructure. This is a classic MageCart web skimmer attack.

execution_context.file_location: Injected JavaScript in payment page (e.g., checkout.js or inline <script> tag)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code hooks the payment form submission, collects credit card details from input fields, and sends them via HTTPS POST to a malicious domain, resulting in payment data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting form submissions and exfiltrating sensitive payment data to an external domain is a hallmark of web skimming attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate e-commerce scripts should only send payment data to trusted payment processors, not to unknown or external domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Form validation or integration with legitimate payment gateways may hook form submissions, but never exfiltrate data to untrusted domains.
key_indicators: Reads credit card fields directly from DOM
Sends data to external, non-payment domain
Uses fetch/XHR to exfiltrate sensitive data

attack_chain.action: Attacker injects malicious JavaScript into the ticket reseller's payment page.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of skimmer code in users' browsers

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript hooks the payment form submission event.
attack_chain.leads_to: Collection of payment card data from user input

attack_chain.action: Collected payment card data is sent to attacker-controlled server via HTTPS POST.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code hooking form submission events on payment pages
Outbound network requests (fetch/XHR) to untrusted or unknown domains from payment pages
Access to credit card input fields in the DOM
file_indicators: Unexpected or recently modified JavaScript files on payment pages
Inline <script> tags with obfuscated or unfamiliar code
References to external JavaScript from non-standard domains
network_indicators: HTTPS POST requests from client browsers to domains not associated with the business or payment processor
Unusual traffic patterns from checkout pages to unknown endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor payment and checkout pages for unauthorized JavaScript modifications, especially scripts that access credit card fields and send data to external domains. Use Content Security Policy (CSP) to restrict allowed destinations for outbound requests. Analyze network traffic for POST requests to unfamiliar domains originating from payment pages. Regularly audit web assets for unauthorized changes or injected scripts.
